title: Multi-Path Pilot Pricing Simulator and Security Dossier
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Overview

This document is a single-stop sales enablement dossier intended for sellers, solutions engineers, and GTM partners engaging technical buyers evaluating Redwood across pilot, dedicated, and private deployment paths. It contains: succinct positioning, persona-based messaging, a compact competitive snapshot, a pricing simulator (worked examples), a repeatable pilot->dedicated migration playbook, a short case study with measurable outcomes, and a scoped Security FAQ for prospect conversations. Use it during discovery, technical workshops, and commercial alignment meetings.

One-sentence position

- Redwood Inference: a production-first inference platform that lets engineering teams reduce per-token cost and operational risk while keeping deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private).

Topline selling points for technical buyers

1) Predictable economics — Reserved/Dedicated capacity and autoscale policies that remove noisy neighbor variance.
2) Consistent runtime — Same API and toolchain across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (reduces lift for engineering teams).
3) Cost controls — Intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations with measurable unit-economics impact.
4) Reliability & fallbacks — Smart routing and automatic model-variant fallback to maintain availability.
5) Observability — Token-level cost, latency breakdown, tracing and rollout tools that integrate into CICD.

Persona-based value messaging

- CTO / VP Eng:
  - Risk: avoid model & infra lock-in, predictable economics for planning.
  - Message: Redwood moves the unit economics from experimentation to production by combining reserve capacity + observability + rollback policies.

- Platform / Infra Engineer:
  - Risk: operational load and tool fragmentation.
  - Message: same API and runtime across environments, integrated autoscaling, and standard rollout primitives reduce maintenance overhead.

- Product / ML Engineer:
  - Risk: quality regressions from quantization and latency spikes.
  - Message: model profiles, quantization guidance, and per-route quality monitoring keep accuracy lifecycles predictable.

Competitive snapshot (short-form)

| Capability | Redwood | Generic Cloud Endpoints | Niche Inference Vendors |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private | Yes | No/partial | Often yes but ops-heavy |
| Reserved low-variance capacity | Yes (Dedicated) | Limited | Varies |
| Developer-first APIs & SDKs | Yes | Yes | Limited |
| Cost tooling (batching, cache, quantization) | Built-in | Manual | Tooling gap |
| Observability (token-level, rollout tools) | First-class | Basic | Depends |
| Enterprise compliance & on-prem options | Yes | Varies | Often yes |

Competitive talking points

- Against generic cloud endpoints: emphasize predictable unit economics, model-aware kernel selection, and turnkey batching/caching to reduce token spend.
- Against niche inference vendors: highlight integrated product experience (console + rollout + SDK) and managed reserved options that reduce total ops cost.

Pricing simulator guidance (how to run in <15 mins)

Inputs required from prospect:
- Expected QPS (average requests per second) and 95th percentile latency target.
- Average prompt + completion token count.
- Target model family / model size (e.g., Llama-3-70B, mix of LLM+embedding).
- Uptime SLA requirement (99.9% vs 99.95%).

Simulator quick steps:
1) Calculate sustained tokens/sec = QPS * (prompt_tokens + completion_tokens).
2) Map to Dedicated instance class recommendations (we provide a lookup table in sales toolkit).
3) Apply batching factor (recommended is 1.8–3x based on workload) to estimate effective tokens/sec and amortized per-token GPU cost.
4) Include KV caching discount (if >30% prefix reuse, apply 20–50% token reduction).
5) Add platform fees + optional private deployment premium.

Worked examples (rounded)

Example A — SMB chat app (pilot -> hosted):
- QPS: 5 avg, prompt 30 tokens, completion 120 tokens => sustained tokens/sec ≈ 25.
- Hosted cost estimate (incl. platform fee): ≈ $0.045 / 1k tokens => monthly ~ $3,240 (for 30-day active usage at given QPS).
- Pilot recommendation: Hosted API with 2-week scaling guardrails and pre-provisioned rate limits.

Example B — Midmarket customer (pilot -> dedicated):
- QPS: 40 avg, prompt 50, completion 200 => sustained tokens/sec ≈ 10,000 tokens/sec.
- Recommended: Dedicated pool (3x p4-equivalent nodes), batching factor 2x, KV cache expected 25% => estimated blended cost reduction to ~$0.010–0.018 / 1k tokens.
- Commercial guidance: propose 3-month reserved commit with a trial discount and an option to convert to 12-month at pre-agreed pricing.

Commercial negotiation playbook (pricing levers)

- Pilot discounts: 20–40% platform fee waiver for 30–90 day pilots (depending on ARR potential).
- Reserved commitment: scale discount based on committed spend volume and term length (12/24/36 months).
- Onboarding credits: include SRE hours (up to 40 hours) and a performance tuning engagement for high-touch pilots.
- Add-ons pricing: longer observability retention, private control plane, and compliance packages priced separately.

Migration: Pilot -> Dedicated (repeatable playbook)

Owner: Solutions Engineering + Customer Success (CS)
Prereqs:
- Signed pilot MSA and data processing agreement (DPA) if needed.
- Observability seed: ingested sample traffic and representative prompt set for quality monitoring.

Step-by-step
1) Discovery & traffic profiling (0–3 days): capture token distribution, latency P95 targets, and cache hit expectations.
2) Recommendation & sizing (1 day): propose Dedicated pool type + autoscale policy + fallback model variants.
3) Pilot validation (1–2 weeks): run pilot on hosted or small dedicated pool; collect perf, cost, and quality metrics.
4) Capacity commit & contract (1–2 weeks): align on reserved nodes and SLA.
5) Cutover plan (weekend window): staged rollout — 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback at predefined error & latency thresholds (error budget triggers described below).
6) Post-migration tuning (2–4 weeks): optimize batching, adjust KV policies, and finalize quantization profiles if used.

Runbook thresholds & rollback policy
- Latency SLO breach: if P95 latency > target + 20% for >10 minutes, shift traffic to fallback variant or hosted pool.
- Error budget: if error rate > 2% sustained for 5 minutes, automatic rollback to previous model version and notify oncall.
- Cost spike guardrail: if token spend > 30% above forecast in 24 hours, throttle non-critical routes and alert finance.

Case study: VelocityHealth (fictional composite for reference)

Context:
- Industry: digital health, HIPAA-adjacent feature set, anonymized clinical summarization for patient triage.
- Initial problem: unpredictable inference costs, latency spikes at morning peaks, and regulatory concerns about PHI residency.

Engagement:
- Pilot: 6-week hosted pilot with sample prompts, quality checks, and end-to-end observability.
- Key actions: enabled KV caching for templates, introduced per-route autoscaling, and applied a quantization profile lowering GPU memory use by 30%.

Outcomes (90 days):
- 42% reduction in per-token cost vs their prior managed endpoint.
- P95 latency improvement from 520ms -> 210ms after batching & kernel tuning.
- Successfully migrated to Dedicated with a private control plane in a single-month cutover.
- Customer testimonial highlight: “Redwood let us ship reliable inference without a dedicated infra team — cost and latency stabilized in production.”

Security FAQ (short list tailored for prospect discussions)

Q: What deployment patterns are available for regulated workloads?
A: Hosted API, Dedicated (isolated GPU pools with per-customer isolation), and Private deployment (VPC or on-prem with private control plane). Private supports HSM/KMS integrations and air-gapped packaging.

Q: How is data residency handled?
A: Customers can pin workloads to region-specific clusters; Private deployment supports full on-prem residency. We also offer contract-level data residency clauses for enterprise deals.

Q: How are keys and secrets managed?
A: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and supports HSM-backed key storage in Private deployments.

Q: Do you log request text or model outputs?
A: By default, request/response payloads are logged for observability in hosted mode but can be redacted or disabled. For Dedicated and Private, logging policy is customer-configurable and can be restricted to metadata only.

Q: What certifications and audits are available?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (in-scope for hosted). For Private deployments, Redwood provides evidence packages and can support customer-provided audits. Reach out to security-ops for details.

Q: How is vulnerability management handled?
A: Regular CVE scanning, periodic penetration testing, and a defined SLA for critical patch application. Customers can subscribe to security bulletin notifications.

Assets & pitch guidance (what to send)

- Pre-call pack: 1-page technical infographic (latency & cost delta), 1-page security summary, and a suggested pilot success metric sheet.
- Post-call: customized pricing simulator export (CSV) + proposed pilot SOW including milestone metrics and success criteria.
- Demo script: include a live token-cost dashboard, a trace showing fallback to a cheaper model variant, and a canary rollback simulation.

Appendix: useful tables and quick references

- Quick size to recommendation mapping (example):
  - <500 tokens/sec -> Hosted trial or small Dedicated node
  - 500–5k tokens/sec -> 1–3 Dedicated nodes, enable batching & KV cache
  - >5k tokens/sec -> Dedicated pool with autoscaling and custom quantization profile

- Typical onboarding items checklist:
  1) Signed pilot MSA + DPA
  2) Representative prompt set upload
  3) Observability ingestion: sample traces, token histograms
  4) Run initial cost simulation and agree SLOs
  5) Schedule cutover window and rollback criteria
